title: Site-derived roadside-grass silage and IFBB press-fluid methane-test summaries
citation: Piepenschneider, M., Bühle, L., Hensgen, F., & Wachendorf, M. (2016). Energy recovery from grass of urban roadside verges by anaerobic digestion and combustion after pre-processing. Biomass and Bioenergy, 85, 194–202. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biombioe.2015.12.012. Values transcribed from Table 11 of Piepenschneider, M. (2015), Urban Grass and Grass-Leaf Litter Mixtures as Source for Bioenergy Recovery, University of Kassel dissertation.
source_locations: Dissertation Chapter 4 Table 11, printed p. 55 (PDF p. 66); sampling and digestion methods, printed pp. 44–46 (PDF pp. 55–57); gas normalization definition, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 9)
geography: Ten urban roadside-verge sites in Kassel, Germany
license: No explicit open reuse license identified for the thesis or article. This dataset contains a limited attributed transcription of published table values; verify rights before external redistribution.
material_scope: Silage from 2-cut and 4-cut roadside grass and IFBB press fluid from 2-cut grass; Table 11 reports sample counts and mean volatile-solids fraction, methane fraction in biogas, and specific methane yield with standard deviation.
experimental_conditions: Silage was ensiled at least six weeks. BMP tests used 400 g chopped silage with 8 kg inoculum and 3.6 kg water, or 4 kg press fluid with 8 kg inoculum. Silage tests ran in duplicate for 35 days; press-fluid tests in triplicate for 14 days at 37±1 C, with intermittent stirring. Inoculum methane was separately measured and subtracted. Methane volumes were normalized to 273.15 K and 1013.25 hPa and divided by volatile solids; the source applies corrections for VS lost during drying.
sample_count_interpretation: Table 11 sample number is the number of site-derived substrate samples available for the given management and harvest. It is distinct from the laboratory digestion replicate count, which is two for silage and three for press fluid.
data_scope: 18 records: three reported metrics for each of six substrate/harvest categories. Means and standard deviations are separated into numeric columns. No new pooled or annualized values are calculated.
limitations: Kassel urban roadside grass is a comparator, not Dutch roadside grass or a GreenHub feedstock default.
Some site/harvest combinations had insufficient biomass for ensiling; the Table 11 sample counts therefore differ among treatments and are not a balanced sample design.
BMP values come from laboratory batch tests, not continuous reactor operation, gas upgrading or full-scale methane recovery.
The source reports no site-level values in Table 11, and this extract does not reconstruct individual observations from means and standard deviations.
Volatile-solids values are tied to the source's drying/incineration procedure and correction approach; comparisons with other studies require method harmonization.
Reference-only. No runtime methane-yield parameter or GreenHub default is activated.
conversion_or_processing: Transcribed means, standard deviations and source-reported sample counts. No unit conversion, pooling, annualization or inferred yield was performed.
uncertainty: Source-reported standard deviations and sample numbers are preserved. They are not converted to standard errors or confidence intervals.
